reasoning: All successfully reviewed files show standard AUR binary packaging practices: PKGBUILD downloads prebuilt binaries from the official GitHub repository (github.com/crmne/zapfast) with pinned SHA-256 checksums, uses standard install commands, and contains no obfuscated code or network exfiltration. The .SRCINFO contains standard metadata with pinned checksums. The zapfast-bin.install script is purely informational (prints post-install instructions). The .gitignore is standard. No malicious injection patterns detected.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement between 'inconclusive' (qwen) and 'safe' (deepseek) was caused by tool errors, not security findings. The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 API error when reviewing .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict despite all successfully reviewed files being marked safe. The openrouter report (advisory only, doesn't count as a vote) had parse errors on zapfast-bin.install and .gitignore. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The actual security analysis across all models that completed successfully shows no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen model: .SRCINFO review failed with HTTP 400 API error
openrouter model: zapfast-bin.install and .gitignore reviews failed with parse errors
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should not trigger 'inconclusive' verdicts when the underlying security analysis of successfully reviewed files shows no issues. The audit tool should distinguish between 'tool failed to complete' and 'security concern found'.

When multiple models review the same files and find them safe, a single model's tool error on one file should not override the consensus security assessment, especially when that file (.SRCINFO) is metadata-only and cannot contain executable code.
The audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback models for transient API errors to avoid unnecessary escalations.
